chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say, whenever death came to any member of his household: 'Say:

There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne; and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.
When the sick person said it, he would say: 'Go, for there is no harm upon you.'

key_terms.التلقين: Talqeen — the Islamic practice of instructing the dying to recite declarations of faith
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ الْعَظِيمُ: The Magnificent Throne — the highest station in Islamic cosmology
key_terms.بَأْس: Harm, distress — used here for spiritual penalty at the moment of death
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The shahada — the foundational declaration of divine unity

ai.seo_question: What should one say when a family member is dying according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via a chain including Sahl ibn Ziyad, instructed his family members at the moment of death to recite a comprehensive glorification of God — affirming divine unity, transcendence, and universal lordship. This practice of talqeen (deathbed guidance) reflects the Shia tradition of preparing the dying with words of tawhid and tawassul. The final words 'go, for there is no harm upon you' convey Imam Ali's reassurance that this declaration serves as a spiritual intercession.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the death presents itself for anyone from his family, so he should say to him, ‘Say, ‘

There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Lofty, the Magnificent. Glorious is Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the seven skies and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the seven firmaments and whatever is between them, and Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Magnificent Throne; and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’.
So when the patient says it, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So go, for there is no problem upon him’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Maymun al- Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would find any member of his family in dying condition, he would ask him to say, ‘

It is Allah, the Most High, the Most Great, alone who must be worshipped. It is Allah, Lord of seven heavens and the Lord of seven earths, all that is between them and the Lord of the great Throne who is free of all defects. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.’
Upon the patient’s saying this, he (the Imam) then would say, ‘Go on. You do not have to worry about anything.’”
